sources.title: The Home of the Blizzard: Being the Story of the Australasian Antarctic Expedition, 1911-1914
sources.citation: Mawson, D. (1915). The Home of the Blizzard. William Heinemann. Chapters 12-13 (full text): https://www.antarctica.gov.au/about-antarctica/history/exploration-and-expeditions/australasian-antarctic-expedition/home-of-the-blizzard-book/chapter12/ and /chapter13/
sources.supported_claim: Mawson's own account of Ninnis's fall, the supplies lost, and his and Mertz's stated reasoning for choosing the plateau route over a descent to the frozen sea; also the account of dog consumption, Mertz's decline and death, and Mawson's solo crevasse fall and return to base.

sources.title: Mawson and Mertz: a re-evaluation of their ill-fated mapping journey during the 1911-1914 Australasian Antarctic Expedition
sources.citation: Carrington-Smith, D. (2005). Medical Journal of Australia, 183(11), pp. 638-641.
sources.supported_claim: Re-evaluation of Mertz's cause of death, arguing against the hypervitaminosis-A hypothesis in favor of severe malnutrition and psychological trauma; basis for the source_disagreement entry on cause of death.

sources.title: Hypervitaminosis A hypothesis (original)
sources.author_or_institution: J. B. Cleland and R. V. Southcott
sources.citation: Cleland, J. B., & Southcott, R. V. (1969). 'Hypervitaminosis A in the Antarctic in the Days of the Old Explorers.' Medical Journal of Australia, 1, pp. 1250-1256.
sources.supported_claim: Original scientific hypothesis attributing Xavier Mertz's death to vitamin A poisoning from consuming husky liver; the other side of the documented source_disagreement on cause of death.

sources.title: Mawson's fatal journey / Catastrophe (Home of the Blizzard interpretive site)
sources.author_or_institution: Australian Antarctic Division / Australian Antarctic Program
sources.supported_claim: Government archival cross-check of the timeline of Ninnis's fall, the supplies lost, and Mawson's subsequent solo journey and near-miss return relative to the Aurora's departure.

sources.title: Far Eastern Party
sources.author_or_institution: English Wikipedia (used for discovery/orientation only; underlying facts cross-checked against Home of the Blizzard and the MJA articles)
sources.supported_claim: Orientation on party composition, dates, and overall sequence of events, used only to identify primary and academic sources rather than as a standalone citation for load-bearing claims.

sources.title: The Most Terrible Polar Exploration Ever: Douglas Mawson's Antarctic Journey
sources.supported_claim: Corroborating narrative detail on the deadline pressure created by the Aurora's necessary departure date and the scale of Mawson's solo trek.

sources.title: Douglas Mawson
sources.supported_claim: General biographical and chronological cross-check on Mawson's role as expedition leader and the dates of the Far Eastern Party's sledging journey.
